Crypto & Silver Collapse, Software Gets Obliterated, & Two Stock Recommendations | The Weekly Wrap

Recorded February 5, this wrap contrasts violent silver and crypto moves with software disruption fears. Eisman introduces new Charter and Meritage positions based on future capex relief, buybacks and possible operating improvement, then examines AI spending and several earnings reports.

YouTube · 2026-02-06 ↗Substack · 2026-02-06 ↗
The Charter and Meritage theses are unusually explicit about their operating mechanisms, but their multiyear forecasts remain unfinished. Charter later results weaken the early stabilization narrative. The capex-versus-cash distinction is useful; high free-cash-flow yield is not a mathematical bankruptcy signal, and less capex does not directly raise current accounting EPS.

  • Price discounts future cash flows, which can differ from the quoted current or forecast numerator.

Assessment test: Model sustainable cash flow, debt service and risk separately.

A continuing cash deficit must be financed or reduced, but stopping one funding source does not logically imply immediate extinction. Debt, strategic funding, restructuring, asset sales or spending cuts are possible.

Conditional reasoning

Loss of one cash source forces adjustment when liquidity is exhausted; it does not alone rule out every adjustment that preserves the firm.

  • The firm has a cash deficit but may alter expenditures or obtain other financing.

Assessment test: Specify liquidity runway, unavoidable obligations and available alternative capital.

How he reasons here

  • A low multiple needs an operating or capital-allocation catalyst.
  • Separate capital spending from earnings and cash generation.
  • Watch how competitive narratives change the reaction to good results.
  • Distinguish a profitable incumbent funding AI from a loss-making firm dependent on new capital.
